task: A strategically located border city that serves as the primary gateway for trade between two rival powers has petitioned for expanded self-governance. The city's merchant council argues that its unique position requires flexibility in tariffs, legal codes, and diplomatic representation that a distant central government cannot provide. Granting autonomy would likely increase trade revenue and reduce administrative burden, but it would also create a precedent that other prosperous cities might follow, potentially eroding central authority. The rival power has signalled that it would view the city's autonomy as an opportunity to expand its own influence there. Design a governance framework for the border city that grants sufficient flexibility to maximise its economic function while preserving its political loyalty and preventing foreign co-option.

dispatches.responsibility: Draft the autonomy charter: define the legal grant, enumerate delegated powers (tariff, legal, commercial), set sunset clauses and revocation triggers, and establish the escalation ladder linking city government to central authority.
Design bounded tariff authority: set ceiling rates, revenue-sharing ratios with the central treasury, audit cadences, and automatic tripwires for debt or customs anomalies.

Define legal-code jurisdiction: specify which categories of commercial and civil law the city may modify, which must follow central codes (treason, security, capital crimes), and the appeals path to central courts.

Bound diplomatic representation: specify which levels of foreign contact the city may conduct, mandatory central notification for higher-level dealings, and protocols to prevent back-channel agreements with the rival power.
Establish the security architecture: central garrison composition independent of city council, limits on city watch size and armament, intelligence reporting lines, and intervention thresholds.

Build the review and tripwire system: standing audit of city compliance, power to seal-and-reject ultra vires city actions, and automatic charter-review triggers when indicators cross defined thresholds.
